title: Developer SDK
summary: Applications build outside the kernel tree against the packaged SDK (toolchain, headers, libraries and disk tool) and run here.

cases.title: The checkout has one SDK build script, scripts/build-sdk.sh, and it is executable
scripts/build-sdk.sh --prefix DIR builds the SDK from a clean clone of the commit, offline, and exits 0
The SDK build prints no compiler warnings (the pinned core library's NEON notice, #945, excepted)
The SDK's VERSION is one line, breenix-sdk <version> <commit>, naming the full commit it was built from
Two builds of the commit from clean clones at different paths give byte-identical SDK trees
bin/aarch64-breenix-cc --version exits 0 and its first line names breenix-sdk, aarch64 and the commit
bin/x86_64-breenix-cc --version exits 0 and its first line names breenix-sdk, x86_64 and the commit
bin/aarch64-breenix-cargo --version exits 0 and its first line names breenix-sdk, aarch64 and the commit
bin/x86_64-breenix-cargo --version exits 0 and its first line names breenix-sdk, x86_64 and the commit
The SDK ships a libc.a for aarch64 and one for x86_64, each holding objects for its own machine only
The SDK ships a prebuilt Rust std (libstd-*.rlib) for both Breenix targets
share/breenix-sdk/rust-fork.toml is the commit's rust-fork.toml, the pinned fork its std was built from
share/breenix-sdk/targets holds rustc target specs with os breenix for aarch64 and x86_64
Each of the 29 ISO C17 headers compiles alone and all compile together with -std=c17, for both arches
Each of the 86 POSIX.1-2024 headers compiles alone and all compile together under _POSIX_C_SOURCE 202405L, for both arches
A program naming 78 common POSIX functions and 20 constants, from every major header, compiles and links for both arches
A compile reads headers only from the SDK and the compiler's own resource directory, none from the host or the checkout
No SDK file holds the checkout's path, the clean clones' paths, the Rust fork's path or the builder's home directory
No SDK file carries musl's marks, and no archive defines compiler_builtins' libm math, a port of musl's libm, or holds its module or sources in metadata, bitcode or data
No SDK file carries glibc's marks (__GLIBC__, GNU C Library, __THROW, libc.so.6, ld-linux, glibc)
No SDK file carries the marks of newlib, bionic, uClibc, dietlibc or picolibc
A copy of the SDK in another directory still compiles and links a C program for each arch

categories.title: a C app built outside the tree

cases.title: The C app's eight source files compile and link with only the SDK's driver, in a directory outside the checkout
No file of the C app's build (sources, dependency lists, objects, program) names a path into the checkout
The C app compiles with -Wall -Wextra and no warnings
The C app is a static ELF executable for this machine (no PT_INTERP)
c-app hello prints "hello from c-app" and exits 0
c-app receives its arguments, including an empty one, and getenv finds the environment it was given
c-app exit 42 ends with exit status 42 and prints nothing
printf and snprintf format integers, strings, characters and floats with widths, flags and truncation
fopen, fprintf, fputs, fgets, fseek and ftell write and read back a two-line file
fprintf(stderr) and printf reach standard error and standard output separately
open, write, lseek, read, fstat, rename and unlink work on a file created with mode 0640
mkdir, opendir, readdir, closedir and rmdir create, list and remove a directory of three files
fork and waitpid return a child's exit status 7
A forked child execv's the app, and the parent's waitpid gets the exit status 3 it asked for
A pipe carries a child's message to its parent, which reads it to end of file
A sigaction handler runs once for raise and once more for kill to the process itself
A signal blocked by sigprocmask stays pending, then is delivered when unblocked
Four pthreads each sum a range and pthread_join returns their results
Four pthreads incrementing a counter 10000 times each under a mutex reach 40000
A producer thread hands 100 values through one slot guarded by a condition variable
A socketpair carries a message to a forked child and its reply back
A TCP server on 127.0.0.1 accepts a forked client, reads its request and replies
A UDP datagram sent between two sockets on 127.0.0.1 arrives with the sender's port
libm's sqrt, sin, cos, exp, log, pow, fmod, floor, ceil, atan2, hypot, cbrt and lround give the expected values

categories.title: a Rust app built outside the tree

cases.title: The Rust std app, a cargo project outside the checkout, builds with only the SDK's cargo wrapper, offline
The no_std app builds with only the SDK's cargo wrapper, taking libbreenix from the SDK by version
The Rust std app also builds with cross-crate fat LTO, which needs bitcode in every rlib of the SDK's std
Neither Rust app's build (dependency lists, lock file, program) names a path into the checkout
The Rust std app is a static ELF executable for this machine (no PT_INTERP)
rust-app hello prints "hello from rust-app" and exits 0
std::env::args gives rust-app its arguments, including an empty one
std::env::var reads the environment it was given, and vars_os counts exactly its three variables
std::process::exit(17) ends rust-app with exit status 17
std::fs::write, OpenOptions append and read_to_string write and read back a file
std::fs::create_dir_all, read_dir, rename, remove_file, remove_dir and exists manage a directory tree
std::fs::set_permissions and metadata report length, file type and mode 0640
std::process::Command runs the app itself and status() returns its exit code 5
Command with piped stdin and stdout runs a child that copies its input back
std::env::current_dir and set_current_dir report and change the working directory
std::thread::spawn and join return four threads' sums, and a Builder-named thread knows its name
Arc<Mutex> counts to 40000 across four threads, and an mpsc channel carries 1..=100
std::net::TcpListener on 127.0.0.1 serves a TcpStream client in another thread
std::net::UdpSocket sends a datagram on 127.0.0.1 that arrives with the sender's address
std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::pair carries a message from another thread
The no_std libbreenix app prints "hello from rust-nostd-app" and exits 0
The no_std app's getpid, file round trip and monotonic clock work through libbreenix
The no_std app's main returns 9, and libbreenix's runtime exits with status 9

categories.title: installing apps onto a Breenix disk

cases.title: The SDK ships bin/breenix-image, and breenix-image --version names the commit
breenix-image install puts the C, Rust and no_std apps onto the suite's disk, every install exiting 0
/usr/local/bin/sdk-c-app, the documented install path, is a regular file on the booted disk
The installed program is byte-identical to the one the SDK built
An app installed without --mode has mode 0755
An installed app is owned by root (uid 0, gid 0)
An app installed with --mode 0750 has mode 0750
/usr/local/bin is a directory of mode 0755 owned by root
/usr/local/bin/sdk-c-app hello runs by its absolute path
env finds sdk-c-app by its bare name through PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin and runs it
sh -c 'sdk-c-app hello' finds the app through PATH and runs it
The installed Rust std app runs from PATH
The installed no_std app runs from PATH
Installing the C app over the no_std app's name replaces it: the name runs the C app
breenix-image remove takes an installed app off the disk: it exited 0 and the name is gone
breenix-image list prints exactly the five installed apps' names, sorted
e2fsck -fn finds no errors on the disk after the installs, the removal and the quick start
breenix-image refuses a program built for the other architecture and leaves the disk without it
breenix-image remove of a name that was never installed exits non-zero
The booted disk carries all five installed apps and each runs from PATH
The SDK ships bin/breenix-new, and breenix-new --list names the c, rust and rust-no-std templates
breenix-new c tmpl-c creates a project directory and exits 0
The c template's project builds unchanged with breenix-build --arch, which prints the program's path
The c template's program prints "hello from tmpl-c" and exits 0
breenix-new rust tmpl-rust creates a project directory and exits 0
The rust template's project builds unchanged with breenix-build --arch
The rust template's program prints "hello from tmpl-rust" and exits 0
breenix-new rust-no-std tmpl-rust-no-std creates a project directory and exits 0
The rust-no-std template's project builds unchanged with breenix-build --arch
The rust-no-std template's program prints "hello from tmpl-rust-no-std" and exits 0
Every template breenix-new --list names builds unchanged, and each program prints hello from its project
No generated project's files or build output name a path into the checkout
breenix-new refuses a directory that already holds a file, exiting non-zero and changing nothing
docs/sdk/quick-start.md has sh quick-start blocks, one breenix quick-start-run line and one text quick-start-output block
The quick start's sh blocks, run literally in one shell in an empty directory, exit 0
The quick start's program, run in Breenix as the doc shows, prints what the doc says it prints
The SDK ships the quick start as share/doc/breenix-sdk/quick-start.md, identical to docs/sdk/quick-start.md
